cases.description: Verify that a disabled account loses access despite holding a signed access token.
cases.procedure:
1. Create a real Redis session for an active Admin.
2. Request the protected subject API.
3. Disable the account in PostgreSQL and repeat the request.
cases.expected: The first request returns HTTP 200. The next request returns HTTP 401. The subject remains ACTIVE.
cases.pre: Production JWT and security filters, real Redis session store and PostgreSQL account lookup. The account initially has ACTIVE status.

cases.description: Verify atomic refresh-token rotation under concurrent requests.
cases.procedure:
1. Create a Redis-backed session.
2. Submit two refresh requests with the same token concurrently.
3. Inspect both outcomes and stored session state.
cases.expected: Only one request rotates the token. The concurrent request follows the grace-period policy without creating a second session.
cases.pre: Real Redis and production session scripts. Both requests use the same live refresh token.

cases.description: Verify persistence of failed-login locking and counter reset.
cases.procedure:
1. Record failed logins for one account.
2. Read the lock and counter at the threshold.
3. Reset the counter and reload the account.
cases.expected: The lock and failure count match the configured policy. Reset clears the counter without an unrelated account-version change.
cases.pre: Production account repository and real PostgreSQL. This case checks persistence, not the complete login endpoint.

cases.description: Verify that SUCCESS audit follows the caller transaction and duplicate IDs are safe.
cases.procedure:
1. Record the same SUCCESS event twice and commit.
2. Record another SUCCESS event in a transaction that rolls back.
3. Count committed audit rows.
cases.expected: Exactly one row remains. The duplicate adds no row, and the rolled-back event is absent.
cases.pre: Real production services and PostgreSQL; isolated fixtures. External provider calls are excluded.

cases.description: Verify independent DENIED audit persistence and rejection of sensitive details.
cases.procedure:
1. Record a DENIED event and roll back its caller.
2. Attempt to record details containing a password key.
3. Inspect committed audit rows.
cases.expected: The DENIED event remains. Sensitive details are rejected, and no additional audit row is stored.
cases.pre: Real production services and PostgreSQL; isolated fixtures. External provider calls are excluded.

cases.description: Verify that a real audit write failure rolls back a compound subject lifecycle change.
cases.procedure:
1. Prepare a subject, manager and related classes.
2. Force the audit database write to fail.
3. Execute archive/reopen operations and reload owner records.
cases.expected: The operation fails. Subject status, manager assignment and related class state retain their pre-operation values.
cases.pre: Real U01/U04/U05/U02 services, PostgreSQL and transactions. Other remote ports are mocked outside this boundary.

cases.description: Verify settings persistence, immediate consumer refresh and stale-version protection.
cases.procedure:
1. Read the material-size setting through its consumer cache.
2. Update it as Admin.
3. Read it again and attempt an update with the old version.
cases.expected: The consumer sees the committed value immediately. The stale update is rejected, and only one successful update audit is stored.
cases.pre: Real production services and PostgreSQL; isolated fixtures. External provider calls are excluded.

cases.description: Verify real RabbitMQ publication after transaction commit.
cases.procedure:
1. Enqueue an email job inside a transaction and roll back.
2. Repeat in a committed transaction.
3. Read the isolated email queue.
cases.expected: No job is visible before commit or after rollback. One committed job reaches the actual queue with its original idempotency key.
cases.pre: Production job publisher and Rabbit sender, real PostgreSQL transaction and RabbitMQ. No worker consumes this test queue; email delivery is not claimed.

cases.description: Verify Redis expiry and ownership of download grants.
cases.procedure:
1. Issue a download grant and inspect its Redis TTL.
2. Attempt access with another account.
3. Expire the grant and retry access.
cases.expected: The grant uses the required five-minute TTL. Foreign or expired grants cannot open storage.
cases.pre: Real Redis and production grant handling. Storage and audit ports are mocked; actual Drive download is excluded.

cases.description: Verify the real worker message path acknowledges work with no remaining delivery row.
cases.procedure:
1. Enqueue an email job for a missing delivery in the isolated broker.
2. Read it without automatic acknowledgement and pass it to the production listener/dispatcher.
3. Recover unacknowledged messages and inspect the queue.
cases.expected: The real handler completes safely. The delivery was acknowledged, so recovery does not requeue it. No email-delivery row or outbound email is created.
cases.pre: Real Rabbit channel, production listener, dispatcher, email handler and PostgreSQL. The listener is invoked directly; scheduled worker polling and actual mail delivery are excluded.

cases.description: Verify duplicate backup delivery does not create competing backup runs.
cases.procedure:
1. Deliver the same backup job concurrently.
2. Wait for the controlled dump to finish.
3. Inspect stored run state and archive.
cases.expected: Only one dump runs. Duplicate delivery preserves the successful run and its archive.
cases.pre: Real backup state persistence and isolated local archive. The dump/provider boundary is controlled; this is not a production restore test.

cases.description: Verify subject archive and reopen across actual owner services.
cases.procedure:
1. Prepare a managed subject with open/draft classes and learning references.
2. Archive the subject.
3. Reopen it and inspect related data.
cases.expected: Archive cascades to relevant classes and releases the manager. Reopen does not restore previous assignments. Enrollment and learning references remain.
cases.pre: Real U01/U04/U05/U02 production composition and PostgreSQL. Remote file, mail and queue ports are outside the tested boundary.

cases.description: Verify that a changed manager assignment takes effect on the next authorization.
cases.procedure:
1. Authorize the current manager for the subject.
2. Change the persisted manager assignment.
3. Recheck both accounts through production authorization.
cases.expected: The former manager loses the subject scope. The new assignment is read without a stale cached grant.
cases.pre: Real current-account authorization and subject scope provider backed by PostgreSQL.

cases.description: Verify database enforcement of unique subject codes under concurrency.
cases.procedure:
1. Prepare two subjects using the same code.
2. Insert them in concurrent transactions.
3. Reload the code from PostgreSQL.
cases.expected: One insert succeeds, the competing insert fails, and one subject with that code exists.
cases.pre: Production subject persistence and actual PostgreSQL concurrency. Account/class/audit ports use the suite fixtures.

cases.description: Verify class creation and enrollment removal/reactivation through real owner contracts.
cases.procedure:
1. Create a class as its subject manager.
2. Remove a student from an open class and request its details.
3. Re-enroll the student and reload the class.
cases.expected: The new class starts in DRAFT. Removal revokes student access. Re-enrollment restores access and reuses the single enrollment row.
cases.pre: Real production services and PostgreSQL; isolated fixtures. External provider calls are excluded.

cases.description: Verify stale class updates and unauthorized enrollment changes are rejected.
cases.procedure:
1. Update a class using its current version.
2. Retry with the previous version.
3. Attempt to remove a student as Teacher.
cases.expected: The stale update and unauthorized removal fail. The committed class name remains, and the enrollment stays ACTIVE.
cases.pre: Real production services and PostgreSQL; isolated fixtures. External provider calls are excluded.

cases.description: Verify the approved semester-removal migration preserves academic records.
cases.procedure:
1. Create the previous schema and seed a class and enrollment.
2. Apply the current Flyway migrations.
3. Read the retained records and exercise current class persistence.
cases.expected: The semester column is removed. Class identity and enrollment data are preserved and remain usable.
cases.pre: Real PostgreSQL, actual Flyway migration history and production JDBC class repository.

cases.description: Verify personal AI-key encryption, owner-only access and disabled state.
cases.procedure:
1. Add a personal connection without calling the provider.
2. Reveal it as its owner and as another account.
3. Disable it and inspect persisted data.
cases.expected: The owner can read back the key; the foreign account is rejected. DISABLED is persisted, and the database row does not contain the plaintext key.
cases.pre: Real production services and PostgreSQL; isolated fixtures. External provider calls are excluded.

cases.description: Verify concurrent MCP write retries share one committed result.
cases.procedure:
1. Send concurrent write requests with the same retry identity.
2. Let both transactions complete.
3. Inspect draft and retry-result records.
cases.expected: One draft is created. Both requests receive the same stored result.
cases.pre: Real PostgreSQL idempotency and mutation transactions. The draft operation is a controlled fixture, not a remote agent call.

cases.description: Verify failed MCP mutation rolls back its idempotency result.
cases.procedure:
1. Start a write transaction with a new retry identity.
2. Force its mutation to fail.
3. Query draft and retry-result storage.
cases.expected: Neither a draft nor a successful retry result is committed. A later request cannot reuse a false success.
cases.pre: Real PostgreSQL and production MCP idempotency transaction boundary; controlled mutation failure.

cases.description: Verify task, quota reservation/settlement and usage records persist consistently.
cases.procedure:
1. Persist and transition an AI task.
2. Reserve 700 tokens, release that reservation and settle 650 used tokens.
3. Reload the quota window and usage summary.
cases.expected: The task state is retained. The quota window and shared usage summary both record 650 used tokens.
cases.pre: Actual PostgreSQL and production AI task/quota/usage repositories with restricted runtime credentials. Provider calls and quota-service concurrency are outside this persistence case.

cases.description: Verify concurrent reservations respect one account quota and settle actual usage correctly.
cases.procedure:
1. Set account quota to 100 and global quota to 1,000 tokens.
2. Start two simultaneous reservations of 70 for the same account.
3. Settle the winner at 40, then reserve and release the remaining 60.
cases.expected: One request reserves 70; the other receives AI_QUOTA_EXCEEDED. Account and global counters match. Settlement records 40 used tokens and 60 remaining. Release clears reserved tokens without changing usage.
cases.pre: Actual U06 quota policy/reservation services and PostgreSQL row locking. Two threads use separate transactions and a synchronized start. Business time is frozen within one day; no AI provider call.

cases.description: Verify the global quota cap across accounts and capacity recovery after release or rollback.
cases.procedure:
1. Set account and global quotas to 100 tokens.
2. Reserve 70 concurrently from two eligible accounts.
3. Release the winner, roll back another reservation, then reserve the full global capacity.
cases.expected: One request succeeds and one receives AI_QUOTA_GLOBAL_EXCEEDED. The rejected account adds no usage. Release and transaction rollback restore counters to zero. A later 100-token reservation succeeds.
cases.pre: Actual U06 quota services and PostgreSQL transactions. Teacher and Subject Manager contend for one global window. Business time is frozen within one day; no AI provider call.

cases.description: Verify publication locks rubrics and student submission creates the grading evaluation.
cases.procedure:
1. Create a graded assignment, answer section and complete rubric.
2. Publish and start it as an enrolled Student.
3. Save an answer, submit it and inspect U08/U09 storage.
cases.expected: The assignment is OPEN and its rubric is locked. Starting again resumes the same attempt. Submission is stored with exactly one PENDING evaluation.
cases.pre: Real U01/U05/U07/U08/U09/U02 providers, PostgreSQL and Rabbit publisher. Remote AI/email/Drive acceptance is excluded.

cases.description: Verify an incomplete graded assignment cannot be published.
cases.procedure:
1. Create a graded draft without complete publication content.
2. Attempt to publish it.
3. Reload assignment state and publication audit.
cases.expected: Publication is rejected. The assignment remains DRAFT and no successful publication audit exists.
cases.pre: Real production services and PostgreSQL; isolated fixtures. External provider calls are excluded.

cases.description: Verify rubric criteria and points survive a real database round trip.
cases.procedure:
1. Persist a rubric containing criteria and point values.
2. Read it through the production repository.
3. Compare its content with the original.
cases.expected: Criteria, item identity and points are preserved without unintended rewriting.
cases.pre: Actual PostgreSQL and production rubric repository. This case checks persistence, not all publication guards.

cases.description: Verify stale saves and enrollment removal protect a practice attempt.
cases.procedure:
1. Publish a practice assignment and start an attempt.
2. Save content and retry with the old content version.
3. Remove enrollment and request the attempt.
cases.expected: The stale save is rejected without overwriting the answer. Removed enrollment revokes access. The saved version remains and no grading evaluation is created.
cases.pre: Real production services and PostgreSQL; isolated fixtures. External provider calls are excluded.

cases.description: Verify API and MCP feedback requests share the same daily reservation limit.
cases.procedure:
1. Prepare two eligible attempts for one account and one remaining daily slot.
2. Request feedback concurrently through the two entry paths.
3. Inspect reservations.
cases.expected: Only one request reserves the remaining slot. The two entry paths cannot exceed the shared daily limit.
cases.pre: Actual PostgreSQL feedback/reservation code and concurrency. Assignment/auth/AI ports are controlled fixtures; no provider request is made.

cases.description: Verify one account reservation does not block an unrelated account.
cases.procedure:
1. Pause an account while its feedback reservation is in progress.
2. Reserve feedback for a different account.
3. Complete both transactions.
cases.expected: The second account reserves independently. Each reservation remains within its own account boundary.
cases.pre: Real PostgreSQL concurrency and reservation service; AI/auth boundaries are fixture-controlled.

cases.description: Verify atomic rollback when evaluation creation fails during individual submission.
cases.procedure:
1. Prepare a completed individual attempt.
2. Reject evaluation inserts in PostgreSQL and submit.
3. Remove the fault, submit again and repeat the request.
cases.expected: The failed transaction leaves the attempt IN_PROGRESS with no receipt, evaluation or SUCCESS submission audit. Recovery creates one evaluation; repeating submit creates no duplicate.
cases.pre: Actual U07/U08/U09 services, PostgreSQL and transactions. An isolated database trigger injects the failure and is removed in finally.

cases.description: Verify optimistic version protection for concurrent evaluation writes.
cases.procedure:
1. Read one evaluation version.
2. Save two different updates concurrently using that version.
3. Reload the committed evaluation.
cases.expected: Only one writer succeeds. The losing write cannot overwrite the winning document or version.
cases.pre: Actual PostgreSQL and production grading repositories/transactions. Service authorization is outside this focused persistence case.

cases.description: Verify JDBC grading writes join the application transaction manager.
cases.procedure:
1. Begin a transaction using the application JPA transaction manager.
2. Write through the JDBC grading repositories.
3. Roll back and reload the records.
cases.expected: The JDBC writes roll back with the caller. No partially committed grading mutation remains.
cases.pre: Real PostgreSQL, actual JDBC grading adapters and shared JpaTransactionManager.

cases.description: Verify class-specific grade-distribution visibility and concurrent update isolation.
cases.procedure:
1. Apply the visibility migration.
2. Update class-specific visibility concurrently.
3. Read each class and stale-write outcome.
cases.expected: Visibility defaults to OFF. One class cannot overwrite another class setting, and stale writes are rejected.
cases.pre: Real PostgreSQL migration and production visibility repository.

cases.description: Verify published individual grades are replaced by a new pending evaluation after resubmission.
cases.procedure:
1. Submit an individual assignment and save a rubric grade.
2. Finalize, try a locked edit, publish and try again.
3. Submit a second attempt and inspect Student grades.
cases.expected: Draft/finalized grades are hidden; publication exposes the score. Locked edits return 409 GRADE_LOCKED without changes. Resubmission makes the old evaluation SUPERSEDED and the new one PENDING; the old score is hidden and audit retained.
cases.pre: Actual U07/U08/U09 services, PostgreSQL and the Student grade lookup service. The assignment allows two attempts.

cases.description: Verify question lineage and draft uniqueness in PostgreSQL.
cases.procedure:
1. Persist question versions within one lineage.
2. Attempt another simultaneous draft.
3. Read the version history.
cases.expected: The lineage contains at most one draft, with ordered versions and preserved identity.
cases.pre: Production question repository and actual PostgreSQL constraints.

cases.description: Verify an unpublished retired quiz reopens as a draft.
cases.procedure:
1. Retire a quiz that has never been published.
2. Persist and reload it.
3. Reopen it and verify its draft/delete eligibility.
cases.expected: Publication time remains null. Reopening restores DRAFT behavior rather than treating the quiz as previously published.
cases.pre: Actual PostgreSQL and production quiz persistence/domain transitions.

cases.description: Verify an empty quiz cannot be published or started by a student.
cases.procedure:
1. Create a class quiz with no questions.
2. Attempt publication.
3. Attempt to start it as an enrolled Student.
cases.expected: Both operations are rejected. No quiz attempt is stored.
cases.pre: Real production services and PostgreSQL; isolated fixtures. External provider calls are excluded.

cases.description: Verify real quiz publication, answer masking and automatic scoring.
cases.procedure:
1. Create a quiz with one valid question and publish it.
2. Start as an enrolled Student and save the correct answer.
3. Submit and inspect the attempt and gradebook storage.
cases.expected: The taking view reveals no correct-answer key. Submission stores the correct score. No grading evaluation is created, and Teacher cannot read the student result endpoint.
cases.pre: Real production services and PostgreSQL; isolated fixtures. External provider calls are excluded.

cases.description: Verify one in-progress quiz attempt per student and quiz.
cases.procedure:
1. Store an in-progress attempt.
2. Attempt to store another for the same quiz/student.
3. Inspect persisted attempts.
cases.expected: The database rejects the duplicate in-progress attempt without replacing the existing one.
cases.pre: Actual PostgreSQL and production quiz-attempt repository.

cases.description: Verify a persisted penalty decision can be revised without losing the raw score.
cases.procedure:
1. Prepare a submitted attempt with an activity suggestion.
2. Save a penalty decision.
3. Revise the decision and reload the attempt.
cases.expected: The final score reflects the current decision. The original raw score and decision data are preserved correctly.
cases.pre: Actual PostgreSQL and production attempt repository. Teacher authorization and browser activity capture are outside this persistence case.

cases.description: Verify group membership uses actual enrollment and whole-set version protection.
cases.procedure:
1. Save a group containing an enrolled Student and its leader.
2. Retry a whole-set write with the old version.
3. Read as Teacher and attempt access as Student.
cases.expected: The group and leader are stored. The stale write cannot remove the group. The Teacher management operation rejects Student access.
cases.pre: Real production services and PostgreSQL; isolated fixtures. External provider calls are excluded.

cases.description: Verify group document sections, locks and submitted snapshots persist together.
cases.procedure:
1. Create a group document and sections.
2. Persist section locks and content changes.
3. Submit and reload its stored snapshot.
cases.expected: Section ownership, lock state and submitted content match the persisted operation. The stored submission can be read back.
cases.pre: Production group repositories and real PostgreSQL with restricted runtime credentials. This is persistence evidence, not a full group submission-to-grading flow.

cases.description: Verify Rabbit-backed event fanout across two application hubs.
cases.procedure:
1. Subscribe two hub instances and a different account.
2. Publish a notice inside a committed transaction.
3. Repeat in a rolled-back transaction.
cases.expected: Both subscribed instances receive the committed account-targeted notice. The other account receives none, and rollback publishes nothing.
cases.pre: Actual RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL transaction and production server-side SSE hubs. Browser/proxy transport is excluded.

cases.description: Verify group submission, member grade publication and grade reset after changed content is resubmitted.
cases.procedure:
1. Create a two-student group and complete a section.
2. Submit, grade, finalize and publish; try root edits after each lock.
3. Change the section content and resubmit.
cases.expected: One group and two member evaluations are created. Publication exposes member grades. Locked root edits return 409 GRADE_LOCKED without changes. Resubmission resets the same identities to PENDING, clears scores and hides prior grades.
cases.pre: Actual U05/U07/U12/U09 services and PostgreSQL. Two active enrolled students belong to one group; the leader submits.

cases.description: Verify group snapshot and evaluation writes roll back together when a member evaluation fails.
cases.procedure:
1. Prepare a group document with completed content.
2. Reject MEMBER evaluation inserts and submit.
3. Remove the database fault and retry the same submission.
cases.expected: Failure leaves no group or member evaluation, submitted snapshot, receipt or SUCCESS submission audit. Retrying creates exactly one group evaluation and two member evaluations with a stored receipt.
cases.pre: Actual U12/U09 services, PostgreSQL and transactions. A test-only database trigger fails a member insert after the root insert and is removed in finally.

cases.description: Verify material queries respect actual subject/class scope and archived-source rules.
cases.procedure:
1. Seed own, foreign and archived materials.
2. Query through production material and AI-reference services.
3. Compare returned identities.
cases.expected: Only eligible materials are returned for each scope. Foreign-class/subject and ineligible archived sources are excluded from new AI selections.
cases.pre: Actual PostgreSQL material repositories and owner access providers. Artifact storage is mocked outside this boundary.

cases.description: Verify replacement history and conditional extraction completion.
cases.procedure:
1. Edit metadata and replace the material source.
2. Complete extraction for the current version.
3. Attempt stale completion/archive operations and reload history.
cases.expected: Metadata changes do not create a source version. Replacement retains history. Stale completion cannot replace the current extracted text.
cases.pre: Real material/version services, PostgreSQL and transactions. Artifact attach is a controlled port; remote storage/extraction job delivery is not claimed.

cases.description: Verify failed module deletion rolls back archived-material moves.
cases.procedure:
1. Prepare a module containing archived sources.
2. Force the module audit write to fail.
3. Attempt deletion and reload module/source rows.
cases.expected: Deletion fails atomically. The module and source-to-module relationships retain their original state.
cases.pre: Real module/material repositories, owner services, PostgreSQL and audit fault injection.

cases.description: Verify announcement HTTP operations enforce ownership, version and soft deletion.
cases.procedure:
1. Call announcement endpoints using real JWTs for each role.
2. Update with current/stale versions.
3. Delete and inspect stored/read-visible state.
cases.expected: Only eligible users can read/manage announcements. Stale changes are rejected. Deleted announcements disappear from reads while deletion metadata remains.
cases.pre: Real security filters, JWT/current database authority and announcement persistence. Session/queue/mail ports are mocked outside this boundary.

cases.description: Verify saved email opt-out does not suppress in-app notification or expose another owner state.
cases.procedure:
1. Save an email opt-out preference.
2. Create a matching in-app notice.
3. Reload preference/notice and attempt a foreign read-state change.
cases.expected: The saved opt-out persists. The in-app notice remains, and another account cannot change its read state.
cases.pre: Real notification service/repository and PostgreSQL. Class/account, job, mail and SSE ports are bounded by suite fixtures.

cases.description: Verify concurrent and duplicate notification delivery preserves terminal SENT state.
cases.procedure:
1. Prepare a pending email delivery.
2. Execute concurrent/duplicate delivery jobs.
3. Inspect sending and persisted delivery status.
cases.expected: The controlled mail adapter is invoked once. SENT remains terminal and duplicate jobs cannot resend it.
cases.pre: Actual delivery state service and PostgreSQL. IMail is mocked; real SMTP/Brevo delivery is excluded.

cases.description: Verify the 180-day notification retention boundary.
cases.procedure:
1. Seed notices around the retention cutoff and their delivery rows.
2. Run retention.
3. Read retained notices and delivery references.
cases.expected: Only notices older than the cutoff are deleted. Only their related deliveries are cascaded.
cases.pre: Real notification repository, PostgreSQL and controlled business time.

cases.description: Verify automatic notification email processing and safe duplicate delivery.
cases.procedure:
1. Accept an enrollment event to create a notification and queued delivery.
2. Start the real Rabbit consumer and wait for SENT.
3. Enqueue the same delivery again and drain the consumer.
cases.expected: The delivery reaches SENT through the production listener and handler. The controlled provider accepts one email. Duplicate delivery is acknowledged without another send or remaining queued message.
cases.pre: Actual U14 producer, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, automatic consumer and production listener/dispatcher/handler. Only the external IMail provider is controlled; no real email is sent.

cases.description: Verify retry through the configured Rabbit delay after a temporary mail failure.
cases.procedure:
1. Configure the controlled mail provider to fail once.
2. Queue an enrollment notification and start the consumer.
3. Inspect PENDING and the retry queue, then wait for real redelivery.
cases.expected: The first failure leaves the delivery PENDING and places one message in jobs.retry.30s. The actual 30-second TTL redelivers it. Two provider attempts yield one accepted email and terminal SENT.
cases.pre: Actual U14 producer, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, automatic consumer and production listener/dispatcher/handler. Only the external IMail provider is controlled; no real email is sent.

cases.description: Verify dashboard composition reads actual owner totals and protects personal data.
cases.procedure:
1. Seed accounts, a subject, a class and enrollment.
2. Load the dashboard as Admin.
3. Compare totals and attempt the same operation as Teacher.
cases.expected: Account, subject and class totals match owner records. No email, password hash or subject identity is exposed. Teacher access is rejected.
cases.pre: Real production services and PostgreSQL; isolated fixtures. External provider calls are excluded.

cases.description: Verify backup status distinguishes empty data from malformed terminal state.
cases.procedure:
1. Query backup status with no runs.
2. Insert a terminal run missing its required completion time.
3. Query status again.
cases.expected: Empty history is available. Malformed terminal data is reported unavailable rather than a successful backup.
cases.pre: Actual U03 backup provider, PostgreSQL repository and Spring transactions. The U15 consumer composition is covered separately.

cases.description: Verify backup summary remains internally consistent during concurrent updates.
cases.procedure:
1. Update backup runs concurrently with summary reads.
2. Read counts and last-success data repeatedly.
3. Check each returned summary.
cases.expected: Each summary uses a consistent snapshot. Counts and success information never come from incompatible states.
cases.pre: Actual U03 backup status provider and PostgreSQL transactional reads.
